title: feat: NovaPay multi-provider payment abstraction layer
author: marcus_rivera
body:
## Summary
Implements the PaymentProvider abstraction that allows swapping between Stripe, Braintree, and future providers without changing the calling code.

## Key design decisions
- Abstract base class `PaymentProvider` with normalized error codes (see `payments/base.py`)
- Provider-specific adapters in `payments/providers/`
- Feature flag `MULTI_PROVIDER_ENABLED` via LaunchDarkly controls rollout (ask Priya for flag access)

## GDPR compliance
- All token storage routes to EU region only (eu-west-1)
- Redis cache TTL hardcoded to 21600s (6h) — under James's 24h limit
- Reviewed by James Okafor on 2024-02-13 ✅

## Testing
- 94% unit test coverage on abstraction layer
- Integration tests run against Stripe test mode and Braintree sandbox
- Load test: 500 concurrent transactions, p99 < 200ms

Related: NOVA-112, NOVA-134

comments.author: priya_nair
comments.body: Infrastructure approved. The EU region constraint is correctly enforced in the Terraform config. One question: what happens if the EU Redis is down? Does it fall back to local memory? That could break GDPR compliance.

comments.author: marcus_rivera
comments.body: Good catch @priya_nair. No fallback to local memory — I added a hard fail with a 503 response if EU Redis is unavailable. Better to return an error than silently store tokens outside EU. Updated in commit a3f92c.

comments.author: james_okafor
comments.body: Legal review complete. The EU-only storage and the no-fallback behavior are correct. The 6h TTL is fine. One thing to add to the PR description: document that this was reviewed for GDPR compliance so it shows up in our audit trail.

comments.author: anika_sharma
comments.body: Frontend integration tested against this branch. The normalized error codes are a huge improvement — I can now show meaningful error messages to users instead of generic 'payment failed'. Approving.

title: bug: Race condition in checkout component on fast transactions
author: anika_sharma
body:
## Problem
When a payment completes in under 200ms (common for returning customers with stored cards), the checkout component receives both a 'processing' and 'completed' webhook event almost simultaneously. The UI briefly flashes 'Processing...' then immediately shows 'Complete', which looks broken.

## Reproduction
1. Use a Stripe test card with no 3DS
2. Submit payment
3. See the status flicker

## Expected
Smooth transition to 'Complete' state

## Discussed in
#engineering-general thread on 2024-02-05

comments.author: marcus_rivera
comments.body: Root cause confirmed: the webhook processor dispatches both events with no delay because they arrive in the same 100ms window. Fix options: (1) debounce in frontend, (2) add 300ms delay in webhook queue for 'processing' status. I prefer option 2 — keeps frontend logic simple. Will implement.

comments.author: anika_sharma
comments.body: PR #291 deployed to staging. The 300ms delay in the webhook queue completely fixes the flicker. Tested across all payment methods. Closing this issue.
